newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Lernout to ship new products.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Lernout to ship new products.

text.p: The chief executive of Lernout & Hauspie said on Wednesday the speech technology company would launch its first "continuous speech dictation" products in the Fall, a timetable accelerated by the recent acquisition of Kerzweil Applied Intelligence.

"We will be releasing our continuous speech dictation products already this Fall and we will ship in the next couple of months," said Gaston Bastiaens in an interview with Reuters. Continuous speech dictation refers to the ability to speak into a devise at a normal cadence while that speech is simultaneously tranlsated into text.
Bastiaens said the $53 million merger with Kerzweil, a company that developed voice recognition systems, was completed on June 26.
Heading the new line of products is VoiceCommand, used in conjunction with Microsoft Word software and designed to recognize spoken words to edit and format documents.

"Then we are going to ship a continuous dictation product for the pathology market in September to eight customers so they can make last remarks on it before we officially ship it in the Fall as well," Bastiaens said.
Bastiaens added that he was comfortable with analysts' estimates that the company's continuing research and development budget would represent 12 percent of its revenues.

The Belgian-based company, which develops speech technology for use in telecommunications, multimeda and electronics markets, posted second quarter operating earnings per share of $0.22 per share, three cents above analysts' estimates. Bastiaens attributed the performance to, "the combination of increased revenue in all businesses and sharp control of costs."
The company's stock added 1-5/16 during trade on Wednesday, closing at 32-3/4.
